en: In the *Praise for the Map of Mañjuśrī’s Guidance* by the Chan Master Fokuo, composed by Zhang Shangying, Secretariat Drafter:
The Ocean of Nature of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra receives the hundred rivers of fragrant water; the Jewel-Light Forest of the Dharma-realm Heaven.
It encompasses the myriad phenomena,
reaches the ultimate true wisdom of the Buddha,
and exhausts the spiritual source of all sentient beings.
Therefore, this "Exquisite Array of the World-Honored One" was compiled by Mañjuśrī,
recited from the Dragon Palace,
and transmitted to Mount Kukkutapāda.
It was subsequently transmitted and circulated, becoming widely known throughout China.
Master Li’s *Compendium* consists of forty fascicles,
and National Preceptor Guǎn’s *Commentary and Sub-commentary* comprises one hundred fascicles.
The Venerable Nāgārjuna’s two hundred thousand verses and Master Fokuo’s fifty-four hymns are the teachings venerated by scholars from these four schools.
If one were to grasp the essential pivot of the great scriptures,
raise up the main headings and sub-items of the Dharma-realm,
and delineate the ritual forms and characteristics of spiritual friends;
This describes the gateway to awakening of Sudhana;
as persons and environments interpenetrate and both phenomena and principle are fully revealed,
the meaning is detailed while the text remains concise.
How can one praise its diagram?
To inspire faith, acceptance, and practice, this serves as the prologue.
When the youth Sudhana first went to the Śāla grove, he...
Section Three: Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
The elephant king turns his gaze;
the lion lets out a roar.
Six thousand bhikṣus attained the Way upon hearing these words.
The five groups of friends were suddenly awakened to their original mind,
attaining the Dharma-door that guides one to fundamental wisdom.
Realizing the ten stages of faith, he praised [the place], saying:
"Leaving the forest, one returns once more to enter the woods; This is precisely east of the temple of the Śāla Buddha."
When the lion roars, the fragrant grasses turn green; where the elephant king turns back, the falling petals are red.
The six thousand mendicants have fulfilled their ten minds; the eminent members of the five assemblies have attained penetration through a single faith.
Cherish this, for our Master has gone southward; across a hundred cities, mists and waters stretch out boundlessly.
The youth Sudhana went for the second time to Mount Supratiṣṭhita to visit the bhikṣu Meghaśrī.
After searching for him for seven days, he finally saw him walking slowly up and down on a separate peak.
Having prostrated and inquired about the Dharma,
he entered the realm of the Buddhas and attained the Dharma-door of mindfulness of all Buddhas and universal vision.
The Verse Praising the Stage of Realizing the Aspiration for Enlightenment:
"Devcun ever dwells upon the peak of Mount Sumeru, Circumambulating its summit with no fixed trace."
Having sought you for seven days yet not seen you, why do we encounter you again this very morning?
Your resolve has awakened, and at this dwelling place, conditions with the Master have harmonized; throughout the gateway of universal vision, the countenances of the Buddhas appear.
Turning my head to gaze toward the setting sun on the slope below, white clouds and blue peaks stretch out in myriad layers.
The youth Sudhana went for the third time to the country of Samudramukha to visit the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha,
who had been contemplating the manifestation of Buddhas in the ocean for twelve years.
For twelve hundred years, he stroked [the disciple's] head and preached the sutra;
though he recalled it and upheld it in mind,
it would be difficult to transcribe even with a collection of brushes.
He attained the Dharma-gate of the Universal Eye and realized the stage of Abiding in the Grounds.
He praised it, saying:
Entering through one door yet arriving at many, returning once more to the gate— Clearly, the Universal Eye illuminates heaven and earth.
For ten years observing the ocean, the profound meaning was realized; Throughout a thousand years hearing the sutras, every chapter remains preserved.
White waves surge with blossoms as an extraordinary omen; The red lotus manifests the Buddha, alone proclaimed supreme.
Even with a brush as large as Mount Sumeru, one could not finish writing it; ten thousand acres of azure waves would break one’s soul.
Sudhana visited the fourth stage on the path to Laṅkā, where he paid his respects to the Bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita.
Moving back and forth through the air, they extensively manifested supernatural transformations:
they stroked the sun and moon with their hands;
smoke and flames issued from their bodies as they traveled everywhere throughout the Buddha-fields, scattering celestial flowers everywhere.
He attained the Dharma-door of Universal and Swift Offerings to All Buddhas.
Regarding the realization of this practice,
he praised it, saying:
Far, far away, he reaches the sea of Laṅkā; gazing into the distance, the scene in the sky is most wondrous.
In every thought-moment, he travels throughout all Buddha-fields; profusely and brilliantly, celestial flowers fall.
With his hand, he touches the sun and moon beyond the three realms; from his body, mist and clouds emerge, veiling the four directions.
If you further seek birth in a noble and happy state, leap like a golden snail over the great waves of the Dragon Gate.
Sudhana, as a youth, for the fifth time went to the country of Dārdapura to visit the elder Megha.
Having asked these questions, they prostrated, scattered incense, flowers, and jewels,
emitted illuminating light,
and distinguished the wheels of syllables.
He investigated the sounds of all categories of beings,
realized the Dharma of Total Retention (dhāraṇī),
and attained the Dharma-gate of the *Sūkṣmasvara-dhāraṇī*.
To praise the manifestation of the noble birth: Incense,
flowers, gold, and precious jewels, Scattered in profusion, afterward reveal his majestic power.
Vibrant light illuminates the three thousandfold world; Expansive speech unfolds the wheel of ten thousand characters.
In dense forests and barbarian lands dwell tigers and leopards; In deep, silent marshes gather dragons and qilin.
From wondrous sounds emerge *dhāraṇī* words, Discerning clearly between Hu and Han people alike.
The youth Sudhana went for the sixth time to the city of Dhanyākara to visit the householder Vimokṣa,
who manifested within his own body the buddha-fields of the ten directions.
The Buddha has no distinct lands; how could there be any difference?
He does not come, yet he comes;
if one seeks to see him, one sees him immediately.
Having attained the Tathāgata’s Dharma-gate of Unimpeded Adornment,
they realized and dwelt in its full perfection.
They praised it, saying:
For twelve years I dwelt in the forest; deep within the woods, I sought those of like mind.
At times I longed to behold the Buddhas of the ten directions, yet I idly observed my own single mind in leisure.
Without coming or going, it is like a flame or a shadow; as conditions arise and conditions perish, the passing of time flows on.
The gates of adornment open; who has come? Along the secluded path, fallen flowers lie and the flowing water is deep.
Sudhana, the youth, for the seventh time went to the country of Mālikā to visit the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha.
After six months of observing samādhi,
fourteen types of meditative objects appeared,
surging forth as hundreds of thousands of signs.
What is not illuminated by the wisdom of *prajñā*?
Having attained the Dharma-door of the Universal Eye,
one realizes the Abiding of the Right Mind.
Praise: The light has already passed through half his body; All day long he remains in profound stillness, as tranquil as a mountain.
From his body emerge fourteen types of radiance, Surging forth from within each pore in hundreds of thousands of ways.
Observing with single-mindedness without rest, contemplating for six months, it was no ordinary task;
the god Māṛīca delighted in the beauty of spring, as willows, orioles, and swallows on the beams warbled their melodious songs.
Thus, Sudhana, the youth, went for the eighth time to the garden of the Sea Tide (Sāgaramegha).
Section Three: The Upāsikā Śreṣṭhadattā.
Her halls and pavilions were magnificently adorned, interspersed with ponds and pools.
Wisdom and compassion function in unison;
birth and death are both destroyed.
Thus, one awakens the bodhicitta.
Awakening to the ultimate vow,
he attained the Dharma-door of the Banner of Peaceful Security Free from Sorrow and realized the stage of non-retrogression.
Praise: Amidst gardens of precious trees and jeweled walls, golden light-webs are spread over golden couches;
the thousand-tiered halls and pavilions are lofty and magnificent, while ten thousand streams and vast ponds overflow with fragrance.
The gate of ultimate vows pervades the entire Dharma-realm;
The bodhicitta is vast, extending through the lands and sands of all Buddhas whom he has served. The high Banner of Peace is the place of rest.
Thus, Sudhana, for the ninth time, went to the country of Nalasa.
3. The Rishi Vimalakṣa and immeasurable other rishis praised him with one voice.
Having descended from the forest and taken hold of the Buddha-field, he realized the true, pure wisdom before his eyes.
He attained the Dharma-gate of the Unsurpassed Banner of Sovereign Mastery over Expansion and Contraction,
and realized the Stage of Youthful Truth (*kumārabhūmi*).
He praised it, saying:
The Rishi Vimala descended from his jeweled couch; He stroked [the Buddha’s] head and took his hand to behold the extraordinary auspicious signs.
The realms of the Buddhas of the ten directions appeared simultaneously; The myriad phenomena, like a constellation spread across the sky, suddenly and fully manifested.
A peerless and wondrous banner rose up in auspicious colors; The *Vairocana* scriptural treasury revealed its spiritual radiance.
Returning to one's original seat to seek the ultimate point, one gradually realizes that one’s lifelong views have been limited.
Sudhana, the Youth, next visited the Brahmin Jvalanāmukha in the village of Iṣādhāra.
He practiced the austerity of scorching his body with five fires;
as doubts arose in his mind, the various devas praised him together,
leading him to suddenly repent for his own transgressions.
Ascending directly upon the mountain of blades and casting oneself into the mass of fire,
one attains the Dharma-door of the Inexhaustible Wheel and realizes the stage of the Prince.
Praise: Seeking a teacher and choosing a friend has been difficult throughout antiquity; Between right and wrong, who can discern amidst ten thousand anxieties?
If one would preserve one's whole body by casting oneself into a mass of fire, One must first exert all effort to ascend the mountain of blades.
Only after the praises of the six heavens do we know its wondrousness; how could it be taken lightly during the time of the five heats?
Dwelling within the inexhaustible wheel as a prince, he resides in a jade tower and golden palace that lock out the mundane world.
Sudhana, the Youth, for the eleventh time, went to the city of Siṃhavijurṇa.
Section Three: The Compassionate Maiden.
Within each vessel of the lion-throne palace of the celestial maiden, adorned with dragon-victorious divine garments, the reflections of all Buddhas appear.
She is able to realize the wisdom that understands the objects of all conditioned phenomena.
Having attained the dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā and realized the stage of consecration,
he uttered this praise:
Controlling cranes and riding clouds, they enter the Imperial Capital; Gradually beholding the true realm, it becomes increasingly difficult to measure.
Within the city of the lion, their voices and forms are exquisite; Upon the dragon-victorious throne, the noble resonance is long-lasting.
Each and every vessel contains a Buddha-land; Layer upon layer of shadows manifest divine radiance.
A thousand gates and ten thousand doors open this morning; Blossoms like clusters of *bīra* flowers fill the hall.
The twelfth visit of Sudhana: He goes to the country of Tryakṣa to pay respects to the Bhikṣu Sudarśana.
The *Dīngběn jīng* (Root Text on the Summit) describes three lines of neck-texture and a circular halo one fathom in width;
the *wàn* character is marked upon the chest, and the golden wheel appears in the palms.
These accord with the capacities of beings and conform to the Dharma.
Without thought and without illumination,
one attains the dharma-gate of the lamp of conformity and realizes the practice of joy.
The Praise says:
Directly entering the city, I questioned the people; Everyone pointed toward Yunlin.
I knew that seeking a friend had led me to the Three Eyes; Suddenly, I beheld my Master’s radiance for a fathom.
Thirty-eight rivers honor the Buddha’s deeds; for hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas, one listens to the sound of the tide.
Why must one speak of being young to leave the household life? A single moment of negligence makes the years and months deepen.
Sudhana, the thirteenth visitor, went to the banks of the River Named Renown.
Section Three: The Youth Īśvara.
The eight classes of beings and the devas of the dragon heavens proclaimed from the sky:
"Ten thousand youths delight in playing together in the sand."
Regarding craftsmanship, arts, medicine, commerce, agriculture, mathematics, and seals,
they attain the dharma-gate of the great supernormal knowledge of skillful arts and realize the practice of benefiting others.
Praise: Ten thousand youths enjoy boundless delight; together they play upon the sands of the river isles.
The sands are incalculable, revolving in endless succession—counted by *ayuta*, *koṭi*, and *lakṣa*.
What use are skill in writing, calculation, and seals? What can be boasted of in medicine, physiognomy, commerce, or agriculture?
If one can realize the light of great wisdom, then the stars and moon filling the heavens belong to the Royal House.
The Fourteenth Visit of Sudhana: To the City of Samudrapāla.
Third: He visited the upāsikā Zu (Zu Youpoyi),
who prepared ten billion seats and invited immeasurable people.
Place a small vessel;
it overflows with immeasurable jewels,
so that all who come from the ten directions obtain full satisfaction.
He attained the Dharma-gate of the Treasury of Inexhaustible Merit and realized the practice of non-opposition.
He praised it, saying:
The city abiding by the sea is lofty and auspicious vapors are dense; Observe further that marvelous phenomena are inexhaustible.
One must know that beyond the thousands of hidden and obscure forms, They all emerge from within a single subtle vessel.
The Four Sages receive the timing to achieve the fruit of sainthood; The Six Classes of Beings, after eating, escape the cage of ordinariness.
Shaolin possesses a distinct, true flavor; the fragrance of flowers and fruit fills the crimson trees.
The fifteenth station: Sudhana visits the Wise Layman in the City of Great Prosperity.
Standing upon a high terrace,
he looked up into the sky as all manner of jewels descended in profusion.
To both the noble and the poor, he bestowed the gift of wealth and the gift of Dharma.
He attained the Dharma-gate of the Treasury for Producing at Will and realized the practice of being unyielding and undaunted.
He praised it, saying:
The myriad phenomena are clear and bright, utterly free from a speck of dust; The Layman Daxing stands upon a high terrace.
Seekers of wealth arrive like a swarm of destitute children; Those of lofty caliber who come to hear the Dharma arrive in endless succession.
Bestowing objects according to their needs, the path of the mind is far-reaching; Giving rise to whatever is desired, the treasury-gate of the storehouse opens.
Ten thousand things and a thousand forms fall from the void; immeasurable humans and devas return satisfied and warm.
Sudhana then went for the sixteenth time to the city of Siṃhaladvīpa to visit the elder Ratnacūḍa.
Holding hands, they observe the dwelling;
within its layered and wondrous pavilions,
they behold the beings of the ten realms.
Having bestowed ten kinds of jewels,
he accumulated a treasury of wisdom through causes cultivated in the past,
thereby attaining the Dharma-door of the inexhaustible treasury.
In the *Huayan shu* (Commentary on the Avataṃsaka Sūtra), it is stated that he realized the "Practice Free from Delusion and Confusion.
A eulogy says:
"Holding hands, they returned home to observe his skills; Upon seeing him once, Sudhana’s majestic presence grew ever more formidable."
Gazing from the top down at the ten-storied pavilions, The Tathāgatas of the three periods occupy the highest tier.
Today, in the human realm, the wondrous fruit is realized; In years past, the Buddhas offered incense and lamps.
If you consider this matter to be something extraordinary, You will have failed the ten-thousand-year-old rattan vine of the Southern Mountain.
The youth Sudhana, as the seventeenth stage of his journey,
went to the country of Vaṃśa and visited the elder Samantanetra,
who prepared incense and medicinal drugs.
With a body of principle and a mind of principle,
they exercise impartial compassion and benefit immeasurable beings.
All these beings are delivered.
This Buddha beholds them all.
They have attained the Dharma-gate of Universal Vision that Delights All Buddhas.
Realizing the practice of the Good Manifestation (Subhūti), he praised it, saying:
"Entering far into the path of the wisteria roots, vast and boundless; How long is the journey toward the Universal Gate and the Universal Eye!"
Body and mind are peaceful and blissful, entirely free from illness; A unique method for harmonizing fragrant medicines.
The dainty delicacies of dhyāna-joy are distributed equally as gifts; Famous robes and superior garments are shared in like measure.
If one wishes to see the Buddhas born from every atom, One should carefully savor the flavor of the pāramitās.
The youth Sudhana, as the eighteenth stage, went to the country of Tāladhvaja and visited King Anala.
The king invited him into the palace.
Carefully observe good and evil;
manifest subduing them so that they may cultivate meritorious deeds and realize that birth is like an illusion, and that an illusion is like birth.
Having attained the dharma-gate of illusion-like phenomena and realized the practice of non-attachment,
he praised [it], saying:
By a single decree of the Banner King, one enters the deep palace; the affairs of the Phoenix Pavilion and Dragon Court are no longer the same.
Swords, halberds, and mountains of blades become sublime functions; cauldrons of boiling water and furnace coals manifest divine power.
Frivolous speech and wicked tongues must be severed; killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct are forbidden and not permitted.
This is the Golden Wheel transforming all under heaven; throughout the trichiliocosm, the wind of Yao’s virtue is stirred.
The nineteenth visit of Sudhana: he goes to the City of Wondrous Light to pay respects to King Mahāprabha.
The luminous samādhi enters into all-knowledge;
dharmas manifest clearly as the various devas surround him.
Adorned with the spiritual lineage, he is an inexhaustible object of contemplation and veneration.
He attained the Dharma-door of the Banner of Great Compassion and realized the practice that is difficult to attain.
He praised it, saying:

In the city of the light of a hundred jewels, all things appear fresh and bright; again, one observes the king entering meditative concentration, wherein mountains, rivers, grasses, and trees all revolve.
Birds, beasts, fish, and dragons all manifest before him;
through the Dharma he gathers and sustains millions upon ten millions of beings, who turn their hearts toward him in devotion as they attend him like many tiers of heavens.
To serve as a transmitter of the Way for a ruler is truly difficult to find; even those of the Ten Stages and Three Sages cannot be compared to such a person.
Sudhana visited the twentieth station, the city of Anala, to pay his respects to the laywoman Acalā.
Those whose bodies are touched by this light immediately attain coolness;
even after passing through kalpas as numerous as motes of dust, they do not give rise to desires.
All various supreme dharmas are unimpeded within their single wisdom.
He attained the Dharma-gate of insatiable seeking for the Dharma and realized the practice of wholesome dharmas.
He praised it, saying:
Her sublime marks and features are peerless in this world; she was indeed that very woman of former times.
Having encountered the Buddha Vimala in past kalpas, she has now attained this conditioned body.
Through many lifetimes, she has cleared the turbid waves of the ocean of desire; her field of mind is a single expanse, utterly free from a speck of dust.
Since the quest for the Dharma has not yet come to rest, one should not begrudge one’s youthful, rosy countenance.
Thus, Sudhana, the Youth, proceeded to the city of Tuṣāra for the twenty-first time.
Section Three: The Pervasive Wanderer (Sarvagamin) slowly ascends the mountain peak;
his physical appearance is perfectly radiant.
Ten thousand devas and ninety-six types of beings observed their vessels and capacities;
they were without dependence and without contrivance.
He attained the Dharma-door of the Bodhisattva’s practice in all places and realized true conduct.
He praised it, saying:
Seeking one another within the city as evening falls, At midnight, I go outside the city to seek you.
The radiant atmosphere gathers upon the blue peaks; In the perfect clarity of form and color, I walk amidst white clouds.
Manifesting bodies according to types, yet not as one or many, You expound the Dharma for the occasion—yet this hearing is beyond hearing.
Within every atom of the east, west, south, and north, all heterodox teachers and celestial Māras are utterly eliminated.
Sudhana, the Youth, for the twenty-second time, went to the country of Vast Extent (Vipula) to visit the Elder Utpalaka.
Gathering various precious incenses, they are blended into a single flavor;
through miraculous transformations, auspicious signs universally permeate the Dharma-realm,
causing all who smell the fragrance to attain the fragrance of the Dharma-body.
Attaining the Dharma-gate of the Fragrance of Harmonization,
one realizes the dedication that is free from the mark of sentient beings.
The praise says:
The *utpala* flowers open toward the sun; Their celestial fragrance fills the refined mind.
The ox-head sandalwood of the Snowy Mountains has all been gathered; From the Elephant Treasury and the Dragon Palace, it is all brought forth.
A single incense stick universally perfumes all as rain and dew; Throughout the ten directions, auspicious signs arise like wind and thunder.
My household does not employ the methods of blending [incense], yet it naturally fills the nine realms with its fragrance.
Sudhana, the Youth, went for the twenty-third time to the city of the Gabled Hall.
3. The Ship’s Captain Vasiṣṭha.
All the merchants together discussed treasures;
they measured and gauged the depth of the ocean.
Whether looking at the moon or observing the stars from afar or nearby,
they know the future and recognize the past,
attaining the Dharma-door of the Banner of Great Compassion.
The Praise for Realizing the Non-Destructible Dedication:
"The daily livelihood is gathered at the city tower; The coming and going of merchants is at the ancient shore."
When gulls and egrets pass by, the marsh grasses along the river are tender; after swallows and geese have returned, the white water lilies are autumnal.
Under the bright moon in the azure sky, one seeks the pearl-shore; upon the windless blue sea, one reaches the treasure-island.
Where is the traveler who beats his drum and rows his oars? His cloud-reaching sails drift away into the distance.
The twenty-fourth: Sudhana went to the city of Rāmāvatī to visit the elder Anala,
who was in the Aśoka grove adjudicating worldly affairs.
May the eight classes of devas and nagas, and all humans and animals, be free from greed, anger, strife,
and contention. May they attain the dharma-gate of effortless supernormal powers in all places and realize the dedication equal to that of all Buddhas.
Praise: For over ten years I have wandered across the four seas; Seeking the supreme path, I arrived at the Land of No Sorrow.
How many demons, beasts, greed, and hatred have been stilled! The eight classes of beings, dragons, and devas have ceased their strife.
Cultivating the bodhisattva path in all places, the ghosts and spirits of the three-thousandfold world-system grieve;
it is solely because of the accomplishment of such power that they can cause weary beings to turn their heads [toward awakening].
Sudhana, the twenty-fifth [pilgrim], went to the country of Śūrpāraka.
Section Three: The Bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavinarditā.
Within King Varaprabha’s Sunlight Garden, there were flowing springs of the eight virtues and precious trees of a hundred flowers.
Each and every head reflects and manifests a body;
one attains the dharma-gate of accomplishing all-knowledge and realizes the dedication of merit to all places.
Praise: The Master’s body has already attained the *manomaya-kāya* (mind-born body), Traveling everywhere through the realms of dust to instruct people.
The springs and pools are the source of spiritual power, beautiful with the eight virtues; The gardens and groves have jewel-trees and a hundred fresh flowers.
In every instance, the mirror of the radiant mind appears; Each turns the wheel of Dharma according to what is appropriate.
Having already let out the lion’s roar for many eons, I know not where he now sighs in distress.
The twenty-sixth: Sudhana, the youth, went to the country of Durgama.
Third: The woman Vasumitrā manifested a true golden color,
and her body emitted radiance.
Whether they manifest before them or come into contact with them,
[beings] remain undefiled and unattached;
realizing that their desires and natures are empty, they all attain the fruits of the Path.
Attaining the Dharma-gate of the Limit Beyond Greed and Desire,
one realizes the dedication of the treasury of merit.
It is praised, saying:
Meeting and greeting, they inquire what karmic affinity exists; The Tathāgata of Noble Conduct offers a single precious coin.
Holding hands and embracing, the moon of the mind is serene; Kissing the lips, the tongue of the precept-jewel is perfect.
Human and non-human women all appear in succession; Heavenly beings and their celestial forms respond without partiality.
The three virtues have already clarified the limits of desire; in wine towers and flower caves, gods and immortals are intoxicated.
Sudhana, the twenty-seventh [pilgrim], went to the city of Śrāvastī.
Section Three: The Householder Vaiśravaṇa.
When the Tathāgata’s stūpa opens, a sandalwood throne appears, and hundreds of thousands of Buddhas all come into its midst.
For those who lack the realization of nirvana,
it is solely for the sake of taming them that they attain the dharma-gate of the limit of non-parinirvāṇa and realize the dedication of roots of goodness.
Praise: Mountains and rivers layered upon one another, the journey grows ever more arduous; Yet reaching this place, the spirit of my life’s aspirations rejoices.
Viśvantara is like the full moon; The sandalwood stupa is as vast as heaven.
He merely observes their types to demonstrate their subduing; he does not perceive the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa.
The realm of samādhi is realized in accordance with [the needs of beings], and the lands of the dust motes of the ten directions are viewed within the palm of his hand.
This concludes the twenty-eighth visit of Sudhana to Potalaka (the *Tala-giri* of the original scripture).
3. Contemplation of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva:
The assembly of bodhisattvas each sat upon jewel-stones, appearing like the full moon.
Performing together with Ciyin,
he preached the removal of fear and transformed beings according to their needs.
He attained the Dharma-gate of the Practice of Great Compassion and realized the dedication that accords with sentient beings.
He praised it, saying:
Winding along, he sought beneath the crags of the western mountains— The *Vajra* jewel, the lunar orb of autumn.
With earnest words, the youth Sudhana asked: "By which path does Avalokiteśvara practice?
How do all living beings escape fear, And how are the hundreds of thousands of diverse species brought to harmony and gentleness?"
Through hearing, reflection, and cultivation, one enters samādhi; yet the barking of dogs and the crowing of roosters do not cease.
Sudhana, the twenty-ninth, here in this very space, visits Samantagupta Bodhisattva.
He emitted great radiance that eclipsed all forms;
as his feet pressed upon the earth, it shook in six ways;
he passed through lands as numerous as motes of dust and served immeasurable Buddhas.
Attaining the swift practice of the Universal Gate,
one realizes the mark of True Suchness and dedicates [the merit].
The praise says:
Majestic within this world’s vast void, his body emits a brilliance from a single pore that differs from the light of the sun, moon, and stars;
its radiance outshines all, leaving the forms of devas, humans, dragons, and ghosts blurred.
Never has he passed through any land in vain, for wherever he reaches a master’s gate, there is transformative penetration.
"May you swiftly travel; I ask you this in passing: the sun is locked in clouds within the bamboo chamber in the east.
Thus ends the thirtieth visit of Sudhana to the city of Drāmiḍa.
3. Mahādeva extends his four arms,
takes up the waters of the four oceans,
and bathes himself therewith.
He manifested precious jewels as an offering to the Tathāgata,
causing [beings] to leave all desires behind and attain the dharma-gate of the Cloud-Net.
Dedication for Realizing the Treasury of Merit.
The praise says:
The four hands stretch long to grasp the four oceans, Bearing them upon the palms and pouring them over one’s head.
Looking back, face and body are pure; Again, one sees heaven and earth, sun and moon, bright and clear.
Cloud-nets and azure banners stack upon one another; Flower fragrances and jewel clusters gather in abundance.
If one attempts to take these things as objects for display, All wriggling and sentient beings find the Way spontaneously realized.
The youth Sudhana, for the thirty-first time, went to the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) to visit the earth goddess Sthāvarā;
each emitted rays of light.
Incalculable jewels all surged forth;
through the power of past roots of goodness, the Buddha’s prophecy was not forgotten,
and he attained the dharma-gate of the treasury of wisdom.
The Dedication of Reaching the Immeasurable Dharma Realm. Praise:
Traveling to Jambudvīpa in Magadha, A million earth deities are arrayed like stars.
With the mouth reciting the Buddha’s records and the mind upholding them all, The feet tread upon the *Saṃghāṭa*, causing jewels to gush forth;
having attained this Dharma-gate, one constantly enters and emerges from it.
Thus observing that kalpas as numerous as motes of dust are not deceptive, one equally dedicates these toward the Dharma-realm, Universally emitting light to behold the *Yamaka*.
The youth Sudhana went for the thirty-second time to the city of Kapilavastu to visit the night goddess Vasanti,
whose body was resplendent with the luminous constellations of the heavens.
When clouds, mist, and darkness appear, the brightness of the sun and moon manifests;
where treacherous and perilous paths exist, they create bridges and roads.
Thus, one attains the Dharma-gate of the light that shatters obstructions and darkness.
He realized the Stage of Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*).
The eulogy says:
The golden crow descends in the west as night releases its radiance; In the land of Kapilavastu, a brilliant splendor appears.
Amidst dense clouds and heavy fog one travels across level ground; With torrential rain from buckets and gale-force winds, one crosses the vast and boundless.
One immediately hangs the sun and moon within the darkness, Then returns to span a bridge over the precipice.
Knowing that many kalpas have already perfected these skillful means, Today we meet—what a cause for joy!
The youth Sudhana went for the thirty-third time to the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) to visit the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā. There,
he attained ten kinds of noble wisdom and the mind of the four dhyānas.
Through the majestic radiance of the Triple Gem and the five meditations on impurity (*pañca-smṛtyupasthāna*),
they opened the gate of renunciation and showed the path of correctness,
thereby attaining the Dharma-gate of universal gait.
He realized the Stainless Ground (*vimalā-bhūmi*).
In praise, he said:
"Delighting in himself, he sought no teacher afar; Without leaving the courtyard, he heard the sound of the tide."
Reflecting back on hearing the wondrous discourse in days past, it does not equal the profound realization attained this very night.
The ten dharma-gates perfect holy wisdom; the four dhyānas distinguish and accord with the Heavenly Mind.
Furthermore, through tranquil stillness one returns to the Way; the stainless flower blooms toward Shaolin.
The thirty-fourth: Sudhana, not departing from the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), visited the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā.
From each and every pore of her body, clouds of bodies surged forth.
Manifesting signs according to the capacities of beings and employing the knowledge of others' minds to lead them into the ocean of liberation—
this is truly a rare and wondrous occurrence.
He attained the Dharma-gate of the Banner of Universal Joy with Great Power and realized the Ground of Radiant Light (Prabhākari-bhūmi).
He praised it, saying:
In every direction, within the innermost sanctum, there are those worthy of your study; yet even with meticulous reflection, none seem equal to you.
Moment after moment, thoughts arise to form an ocean of mindfulness; body after body, manifestations appear as clouds of forms.
The knowledge of others' minds is a wondrous wisdom that is not wisdom; the divine ear hears what is heard and what is unheard.
Having labored diligently for many kalpas to seek the Great Function, his power now suddenly transcends all others.
Sudhana, the thirty-fifth [pilgrim], is present within this assembly;
he visits the Night Goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, who brings universal salvation to all sentient beings.
Light radiates from his two eyebrows and extends from his body to the crown of his head;
this is the realm of a Great Being.
Knowing that the Buddha has appeared in the world, Universal Radiance gives rise to the aspiration for enlightenment through his wondrous eye.
He attained the Dharma-gate for taming sentient beings and realized the Stage of Blazing Wisdom (Arciṣmatī-bhūmi).
He praised it, saying:
At the time of the consecration, the brush-tip is extended within the brows; The samādhi of the pure wheel merges with this discourse on the realm of mind, where layers upon layers manifest.
As the Buddha’s radiance is explained, one gradually comes to know it;
O Wondrous Eye, how could my own body be any different? O Jewel King Maitreya, have no further doubt.

Where now are Samantabhadra and Samantajvālā? With snow filling the vast sky and flowers blooming on every branch—this is the thirty-sixth station of Sudhana, the Youth, within the site of enlightenment:
he visits the Night Goddess Śāntamukhīsamudrā.
In every thought-moment, they give rise to a boundlessly great heart of joy,
and they bring forth the immeasurable Dharma-treasury and the meaning of the Dharma of great compassion,
like clouds and like oceans.
Having attained the Dharma-gate of the Adornment of Vast and Great Joy,
one realizes the Stage of Presence (*Abhimukhī-bhūmi*).
It is praised, saying:
A multitude of millions of koṭis of monks surrounds my body; From a new lotus on a mani-bannered throne, it emerges.
From moment to moment, joy has been born; Every thought and every heart gives rise to the truth wherever it touches.
I see myself and observe immeasurable realms; They form clouds and oceans due to causes from the past.
Briefly stated, the teachers and friends encountered were few or many; the Tathāgatas of the two lands were old acquaintances.
Sudhana, at thirty-seven, went into the assembly of the Tathāgata to pay respects to the Night Goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsambhava.
Universally manifesting physical forms to expound the treasury of the Buddha-dharma,
his wisdoms of hearing, contemplation, and cultivation respond secretly to the capacities of all beings,
causing all sentient beings to guard the city of their own minds.
Having attained the Dharma-gate of the Profound, Sovereign, and Wondrous Sound,
and having realized the Ground Difficult to Conquer (*sudurjayā-bhūmi*),
he uttered this praise:
Within the light of the precious throne, you manifest your body everywhere; Again opening the Buddha-treasury, you deliver all living beings.
I contemplate the boundless reaches of the Dharma-realm: Who would believe that the *dhāraṇī* benefits those who practice it?
The name of the Dharma-wheel is proclaimed once more; Through hearing, reflection, and cultivation, its wisdom is further expounded.
Although this "Exquisite Sound" is a rhythmic composition of the Hu (Central Asian) tradition, its melody emerges fresh like the "Yangchun" and "Snow" melodies.
This is the thirty-eighth [chapter], where the youth Sudhana visits the assembly of the Buddha and encounters the Night Goddess who presides over the blossoming woodlands;
the *Kai-fu-mu-ben-jing* (Sutra of the Blossoming Woodland Roots) refers to her as the "Goddess of Tree Flowers."
Manifesting bodies according to the minds [of beings],
they cause all to perceive and see the closing of the lotus petals that cover the perilous and evil paths;
they rescue and deliver sentient beings, causing them to sever the net of craving.
He attained the Dharma-gate of the Radiance of Vast and Great Joy and realized the Ground of Far-Going (Dūraṃgamā).
He praised it, saying:
When the flowers of birth in the darkness have all been gathered in, do not let them be driven along perilous paths;
after the net of delusion has been destroyed by the sword and the dense forest of craving subdued by the mallet,
when the Mountain King of Wisdom rises as the sun of transformation, the maiden of Jewel Radiance awakens her resolve.
Calculating it, many kalpas have already passed; meeting on such a distant land is truly wondrous and profound.
Sudhana, the youth, for the thirty-ninth time, went to the site of enlightenment to visit the Night Goddess who Protects Sentient Beings through the Power of Great Vows and Diligence.
Appearing spontaneously according to circumstances,
manifesting as one body or many bodies with wondrous form and wondrous wisdom like the sun and the moon,
they universally save transgressors so that they attain the purity of the mind’s eye.
He attained the dharma-gate of teaching and transforming sentient beings to cause them to give rise to roots of goodness,
and realized the Immovable Ground (*acalā-bhūmi*).
He praised it, saying:
In his youth, the Prince saved those condemned to death; now he manifests a manifold body throughout the universe.
The hearts of ten thousand lay devotees are freed from defilement; their eyes, numbering ten billion nayutas, are severed from dust.
His wondrous form is as pure and bright as the autumn sky; his wheel of wisdom shines like the newly risen sun.
After the Buddha Ratnaprabha emerged from the forest, he again beheld the *tāṇḍava* flower through several springs.
Sudhana, for the fortieth time, went to the Pīlava Garden to visit the Night Goddess Viśuddhamati.
Universally observing all Buddhas of the ten directions, they were once nursing mothers in past kalpas; today, as gardeners,
they have awakened to the treasury of birth and are born into the family of the Tathāgata,
attaining the Dharma-door of mastery over birth.
He realized the Stage of Excellent Intelligence (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*).
In praise, he said:
"Having encountered Your direct words regarding the causes of rebirth, I have immediately become one of the family of the Tathāgata."
In a single thought, one contemplates Buddhas as numerous as motes of dust; The ten directions together behold the descent of their majestic spiritual power.
If you wish to know the master of today’s grove, It is none other than the very body of the nursing mother of yore.
There is something else in this world never seen before: With every step and every movement, a fresh flower blooms.
The youth Sudhana, for the forty-first time, went to the Dharma-realm Lecture Hall to visit the Śākya maiden Gopā.
Ten thousand palace deities all came forth to welcome and praise him as he appeared before her, in accordance with the natural law of reality (*dharmatā*).
In the past, through the causal conditions of the Buddha Gandhāra-kūṭa in the garden,
he attained the Bodhi-wisdom of seed-intelligence and realized the Dharma-gate of the Ocean of Samādhis of Contemplation,
thereby attesting to the stage of the Cloud of Dharma.
The eulogy says:
While wandering through the Dharma-realm lecture hall, I encountered the maiden Gopā;
we did not merely discuss the myriad matters before our eyes, but also spoke of the vast merits accumulated over many kalpas of dust.
The Dharma-clouds drift and spread over the myriad peaks; The net of teaching is cast wide, filling the great void.
To examine the human condition is truly laughable— In the garden of fragrant sprouts, the apricot blossoms are red.
Sudhana Kumāra, for the forty-second time, arrives in this world-system.
Third: The Holy Queen Mother Māyā sat upon a precious lotus flower within a great multi-storied pavilion;
her physical form was dignified and majestic, and her radiant splendor was manifest.
In every thought-moment, the Buddha is born; in every birth, she is my mother.
She has attained the Dharma-door of the illusory birth through the wisdom of great vows.
In praise, it is said:
How could I have approached to ask the way? The Rākṣasī guarding the hall explained it again and again.
Gazing from afar at the layered wonders of the towers and pavilions, I suddenly beheld the fresh petals of the lotus.
In every thought, may I become the mother of all Buddhas; in every birth, may I manifest as the body of a queen.
How pitiable is the heart that contains such great magnanimity, encompassing all beings within the worlds as numerous as motes of dust!
Sudhana, the Youth, for the forty-third time, proceeded to the Heaven of the Thirty-three.
Third: The Celestial Maiden Light of the Lord of Heaven has passed through as many eons as there are motes of dust, serving Buddhas as numerous as motes of dust,
upholding their Dharma teachings without ever forgetting them.
Beneficial compassion and wisdom manifest before them without exception;
they attain the Dharma-gate of unimpeded mindfulness and pure adornment.
It is praised, saying:
The Great Lord of the Heaven of the Thirty-three, Whose causal conditions were first formed in the Blue Lotus Realm in an unknown era;
Having attained the perfection of his realization within the wondrous moonlight,
He has already endured immeasurable kalpas of diligent toil, And practiced for many years until awakening.
Within the realm of Jambudvīpa, people inquire of one another; all dharmas are now manifest before them.
Sudhana, the youth, for the forty-fourth time, went to the city of Kapilavastu.
3. The youth teacher Piyamitra immediately pointed him away without uttering a single word,
manifesting that there is no dharma— true dharma is non-attainment, which is itself attainment.
To have passed through this place in vain makes the path ahead no easy matter.
Formerly I heard your name;
this morning I behold you in person.
The eulogy says:
Seeking me from ten thousand miles away, you spoke not of yourself; Yet you claimed that others had mastered all arts and skills.
If people everywhere were suddenly like this, Could my life’s journey have been anything other than by chance?
To transmit the Way and friends is but a false claim; to speak of "masters" and "guides" is a hollow tradition.
Having already laid bare my heart and liver, I seek out those of true knowledge; I reckon that there must surely be a karmic affinity ahead.
Sudhana, the forty-fifth, does not leave his current place.
Section Three: The youth Śālistamba, through unimpeded wisdom, mastered all worldly arts;
he chanted the various phonemes and entered into all gateways of the Dharma.
Regarding the sounds of birds and beasts, clouds and mists, and the seasonal climates,
one attains the Dharma-gate of the Bodhisattva’s Knowledge of Characters for Skillfully Knowing All Arts.
It is praised, saying:
I have heard that you, our Master, are fully accomplished in all arts; meeting you now, I pray you will explain them for me.
Each word of the *Ātāpana* is profound and true; every character of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* is a definitive exposition.
After these forty-two gates are disseminated, they shall be transmitted throughout the three thousandfold world-system through all time.
How is it that the great illumination of the single wisdom is thus? The clouds disperse across the vast sky and the moon is perfectly full.
Sudhana, the Youth, for the forty-sixth time, went to the city of Potalaka.
Section Three: The Upāsikā Bhadraśrī.
Her mind was spontaneously enlightened and she brought benefit and happiness to sentient beings.
From the nature of her eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and intellect, meritorious virtues were produced.
Universally manifesting radiance,
he attained the Dharma-gate of the Bodhimanda of Non-reliance and praised it, saying:
Self-opened, self-liberated, and manifesting for others, One immediately turns toward the red dust of the world to benefit sentient beings.
The eyes, ears, and nose contain a mass of meritorious virtues; The tongue, body, and mind manifest the radiance of wisdom.
Able to give birth and able to emerge, the gateway and courtyard are tranquil; Infinite and without dependence, the realm is pure.
Having realized the place where the site of enlightenment is perfected, with a single body of sword-like brilliance,
he brings about peace and prosperity. Sudhana, the Youth, the forty-seventh,
went to the city of Utpalāvatī to visit the elder Dṛḍhamati.
For hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas,
he has diligently sought the True Dharma at the abodes of the Buddhas of the ten directions without ever resting;
he is a great lion’s roar and a vast accumulation of merit and wisdom.
He attained the Dharma-gate of the Adorned Purity of Unattached Mindfulness.
In praise, he said:
"Those who are diligent are rare, while the indolent are many; The Master’s devotion to the Way of the Dharma is perfectly harmonious."
The Buddhas of the ten directions never cease their activity; For a hundred kalpas, body and mind have experienced weariness.
After the clouds depart from the summit of a ten-thousand-fathom peak, A crane comes to perch atop a thousand-fathom pine.
I pity myself for dwelling in this world of purity; Flowers fall upon the quiet courtyard, where long green sedge grows.
The forty-eighth, Sudhana, was in this very city;
he visited the elder Sucandra,
who did not discuss the meaning of the Dharma.
To briefly indicate the names:
within non-attainment there is further nothing to be attained;
this very non-attainment is itself also non-attainment.
This is called true attainment.
Having attained the Dharma-gate of the Radiance of Pure Wisdom,
he uttered this praise:
The noble person of Wondrous Moon again points to him— That former friend has also passed away in vain.
Reflecting back, the words from both places were few; Yet one laughs at how the paths spread throughout all quarters.
When the flame of sorrow shines with brilliance, do not seek understanding through speech; How can the liberation of the light of wisdom be described?
If you do not now act as a messenger to convey news, the white jade remains flawless though it be polished by itself.
Sudhana, the youth, for the forty-ninth time went to the city of Utpalā and visited the elder Anupamarāja.
He bestowed two teachings as an introduction and guidance,
through which he beheld immeasurable Buddhas.
One attains the inexhaustible treasury and awakens to its underlying principle;
this is indeed a direct shortcut.
Attaining the Dharma-gate of the Inexhaustible Mark, he praised it, saying:
"Traversing afar, one enters the City of Birth; At the gateway of the bustling marketplace, one speaks of the Way."
I thank my teacher for these two lines; yet I reflect deeply that my path has a thousand leagues.
How could I have attained the immeasurable treasury? Through whom was it awakened? Having seen through all lofty men, one should naturally understand for oneself.
As I rise from an autumn dream upon a pine bed at night, the stars and moonlight illuminate the eaves and rafters.
The fiftieth station for the youth Sudhana is the village of this very city.
There he visits the brahmin Paramaśānta,
from whom he resolves to never regress in his aspiration for bodhicitta.
Regarding the past, present, and future, those who have already fallen away or will fall away—
whatever they do according to their wishes shall all be fully accomplished.
They attain the dharma-gate of truthful speech.
Praise: In the village south of the city is the Dharma-gate named Dīpa; Hearing it, may one rejoice with an undeluded mind.
In the past, through sincerity, he attained liberation; In the future, by means of this teaching, he shall attain Bodhi.
Accomplishing all according to the mind and wherever one is, Without retreat and without obstruction, the ultimate goal is the same—this must be believed.
In the second and third months of the Southland, Amidst the fragrance of a hundred flowers, the partridge cries.
Sudhana, the Youth, for the fifty-first time visited the city of Citrarathā.
Section Three: The Youth Guṇakara and the Maiden Guṇavatī give rise to wisdom and compassion through illusion;
they perceive and know one another through the conditions of their mutual affinity.
Ignorance and afflictions,
the land and its sentient beings—
the environment and its inhabitants— are equally empty.
All are identical to an illusion;
they attain the Bodhisattva’s Dharma-door of illusory dwelling.
Praise, saying:
Virtue and the one possessing virtue are harmoniously blended; Both illusory and identical, their intent is inexhaustible.
Dwelling together and practicing together, they achieve liberation; Sharing compassion and wisdom, they manifest spiritual power.
With shared conditions and shared thoughts, their minds are in profound accord; With shared views and shared knowledge, the Way flows through them freely.
If one wishes to attain the fruit of Buddhahood in a single lifetime, Vairocana’s pavilion lies within the South.
Sudhana, the Fifty-second [visitor], went to the Pavilion of the Vairocana Treasury.
3. Maitreya Bodhisattva stood before the gate, having arrived from afar;
he prostrated himself and entered the wondrous realm of contemplation.
Layer upon layer they manifest;
Buddha after Buddha is fully revealed.
Having emerged, they return to closure.
Beyond the reach of thought,
one attains the Dharma-gate of the realm of the Buddha-fruit throughout the three periods of time.
In praise, it is said:
Standing for a brief moment before the gate of the pavilion, the Master of the Dragon Flower returns from afar.
Not only does he contemplate the profound and wondrous by snapping his fingers, but he also listens to the subtle and gentle sounds of his compassionate voice.
Wisdom, principle, conduct, and practice constitute his sun and moon; the bodhicitta is the pivotal axis of the Way.
Where do these many realms come from and go? A single wild goose flies across ten thousand miles of sky.
The youth Sudhana, for the fifty-third time, went into the assembly of the Buddha to visit Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Riding upon the white elephant king and seated on a red lotus throne,
he single-mindedly approaches [the Buddha] to inquire about and hear the essential points of the Dharma;
his wisdom and compassion are perfected.
When the practice and vows have reached fulfillment,
one immediately attains the virtues of a Buddha,
manifesting as identical to the ocean of fruition.
He attained as many dharma-gates of samādhi as there are atoms in all Buddha-fields.
He praised [the Master] saying:
"One hundred and one yojanas away, he bestows his hand upon my head; With a single thought, I am able to see the Teacher Samantabhadra."
Majestic, you now sit upon the red lotus throne; Stately and distinct, you are the white elephant cub.

When wisdom and compassion have finally reached fulfillment over kalpas as vast as space, And when the vows and practices, as numerous as motes of dust, are perfectly complete— The Buddha’s ocean of merit is proclaimed once more;
Yet it is sorrowful to see its waves rolling on, ever more vast and boundless.
In the past, Chan Master Fogu resided at Gui Temple;
now he is in Fengcheng.
Observe how the youth Sudhana visited various spiritual teachers without ever ceasing his journey.
"Behold! Directly accept this and suddenly awaken;
rest, and the Great Function manifests before you.
Praise, saying:
The time has already slipped away; alas, how much you have wandered throughout your life!
More than fifty people have all come to inquire after you, passing through every one of the hundred-layered city walls.
Now that you have arrived here, cease all discrimination—can you directly accept this?
If it were suddenly said that he went north or south, it would be as clear as a chicken egg passing over Silla.
